reasons: Used by every Python gate in the quality check.

terms.meaning: the standard Python file that describes a project's packaging and tool settings
the tool that turns the project into an installable package
a packaged, installable form of a Python project
a fast Python linter that checks style and common mistakes
a label on a test that lets the runner select or skip it

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Project, dependencies, and test settings
sections.what: Describes the project, its Python range, the runtime and development packages, the schedule3d command, the package folder, the pytest settings, and the ruff rules.
sections.why: Likely reason: one file controls packaging and tool behaviour for the whole backend.
sections.watch_out: The ruff rule list and the pytest marker list must match what the tests actually use.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Type checking settings
sections.what: Sets the mypy type checker to strict mode for the schedule3d package and ignores missing type information for three libraries.
sections.why: Likely reason: strict checking catches more mistakes, and the three libraries do not ship type information.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new library without type information may need another ignore entry.

summary: The Python project definition. It names the project schedule3d version 0.2.1, requires Python 3.12 or 3.13, pins the runtime and development libraries, defines a schedule3d command, and sets up tests, linting, and type checking.
purpose: Describes how the Python backend is packaged, what it needs, and how its tools behave.
why: Likely reason: pinned versions make installs repeatable. Other choices are not explained in the code.
how: uv and pip read the dependency lists. The build tool packages the backend folder. Pytest, ruff, and mypy read their own sections for their rules.
inputs: Dependency versions from the package registry and the lock file.
outputs: The installed Python environment, a packaged wheel, and the settings used by the tools.
risks: The pins must stay in step with uv.lock. The private golden tests are marked but not included, so they cannot run in this project.
debug: If an install fails, compare the pinned versions with uv.lock. If ruff reports line length, the limit is 100. If pytest reports an unknown marker, check the markers list.
